\paragraph*{Tables.} All values in the following tables are reported in units of $\times 10^{-2}$; within each row, the better value between $\hat{\mathbf{A}}^\dagger(t)$ or $\hat{\mathbf{A}}^*(t)$ is highlighted.


\begin{enumerate}
    \item When $\rho=0$, there is almost no difference between iid estimation $(\hat{\mathbf{A}}^\dagger(t), \hat{\bb}^\dagger)$ and paired estimation $(\hat{\mathbf{A}}^*(t), \hat{\bb}^*)$.
    \item The larger the $\rho$ is, the better the paired estimation $\hat{\mathbf{A}}^*(t)$ is than iid $\hat{\mathbf{A}}^\dagger(t)$.
    \item The larger the $\rho$ is, the harder it is to estimate both $\bb$ and the correlation $\rho$.
    \item All estimation errors generally decrease as $n$ increases.
\end{enumerate}
